los.html:
Anatomical positionStanding upright, facing forwards, eyes level, arms by the sides with palms forward (forearms supinated), feet together pointing forwards.
Why it mattersEvery directional term refers to this posture, whatever position the patient is actually in.
PlanesSagittal (median = midline, splits right/left); coronal/frontal (front/back); transverse/axial (upper/lower).
Paired termsAnterior/posterior (ventral/dorsal); superior/inferior (cranial/caudal); medial/lateral; proximal/distal; superficial/deep.

los.text: Demonstrate the bony and cartilaginous landmarks visible or palpable on abdominal examination
los.html:
LandmarkLevel / use
Xiphoid processT9; top of the abdomen in the midline
Costal marginCartilages 7–10; lowest point (10th cartilage) marks the subcostal plane, L3
Tip of 9th costal cartilageTranspyloric plane, L1; right side = fundus of gallbladder
Highest point of iliac crestsSupracristal plane, L4: lumbar puncture landmark
Tubercles of iliac crestsIntertubercular plane, L5
Anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS)Lateral end of inguinal ligament; McBurney's point
Pubic tubercle and symphysisMedial end of inguinal ligament; hernias: inguinal above-medial, femoral below-lateral to the tubercle
UmbilicusAbout L3/4 (variable); T10 dermatome
Transpyloric plane (L1): pylorus, gallbladder fundus, neck of pancreas, renal hila, DJ flexure, origin of the SMA.

los.text: Describe the organisation of the parietal and visceral peritoneum, and the principle organisation of the peritoneal cavity, including the lesser and greater sacs, mesenteries, and peritoneal 'ligaments'
los.html:
Parietal peritoneumLines the abdominal wall; somatic nerves (same as the overlying wall, T7–L1) so pain is sharp and well localised.
Visceral peritoneumCovers organs; autonomic visceral afferents, sensitive to stretch and ischaemia; pain is dull and poorly localised (midline).
Peritoneal cavity
  • a potential space with ~50–100 mL fluid.
  • Closed in males
  • in females it opens to the exterior via the uterine tubes.
Greater sacThe main compartment.
Lesser sac (omental bursa)Behind the stomach and lesser omentum; opens into the greater sac only through the epiploic foramen (of Winslow).
Epiploic foramen boundaries
  • Anterior = free edge of lesser omentum (portal triad)
  • Posterior = IVC
  • Superior = caudate lobe
  • Inferior = 1st part of duodenum.
MesenteryDouble fold of peritoneum tethering gut to the posterior wall and carrying its vessels, nerves and lymphatics (small bowel mesentery, transverse and sigmoid mesocolon, mesoappendix).
Omenta
  • Lesser (liver → lesser curvature and 1st part of duodenum)
  • Greater (hangs from the greater curvature, folds back to the transverse colon; walls off infection).
Peritoneal "ligaments"
  • Double folds joining organs: falciform (contains ligamentum teres, the old umbilical vein)
  • Gastrosplenic
  • Splenorenal (splenic vessels, tail of pancreas)
  • Coronary and triangular (liver to diaphragm).
Retroperitoneal (SAD PUCKER)Suprarenals, Aorta/IVC, Duodenum (2nd–4th parts), Pancreas (not tail), Ureters, Colon (ascending/descending), Kidneys, oEsophagus, Rectum.
Fluid collectsSupine → hepatorenal pouch (Morison's); upright → rectovesical or rectouterine pouch (of Douglas).

los.text: Locate the stomach, liver, spleen, omenta, duodenum, jejunum and ileum of the small intestine, caecum, appendix, ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid parts of the colon (and the rectum) within the abdomen using surface anatomy landmarks as well as descriptive abdominal regions and common incision sites
los.html:
OrganSurface position
LiverRight hypochondrium/epigastrium; upper border ~5th intercostal space; lower edge along right costal margin; moves down on inspiration
Gallbladder fundusRight 9th costal cartilage tip, midclavicular line (Murphy's sign)
StomachLeft hypochondrium/epigastrium; cardia T11 behind left 7th costal cartilage; pylorus at L1 just right of midline
SpleenLeft hypochondrium under ribs 9–11, long axis along the 10th rib; palpable only when ~3× enlarged, grows towards the RIF
DuodenumC-shape around head of pancreas, L1–L3; DJ flexure at L2 left
Jejunum / ileumJejunum upper left; ileum lower right and pelvis
Caecum and appendixRight iliac fossa; appendix base at McBurney's point (1/3 from ASIS to umbilicus)
ColonAscending right flank; transverse hangs to umbilicus or lower; descending left flank; sigmoid left iliac fossa → rectum at S3

Regions and incisions

9 regionsTwo midclavicular lines + subcostal and intertubercular planes: hypochondria, epigastric, lumbar (flanks), umbilical, iliac fossae, hypogastric (suprapubic).
4 quadrantsMedian plane + transumbilical plane.
Incisions
  • Midline (laparotomy, through the avascular linea alba)
  • Kocher's (right subcostal: gallbladder)
  • Lanz/gridiron (RIF: appendix)
  • Pfannenstiel (suprapubic transverse: caesarean, pelvis)
  • Rooftop/chevron (bilateral subcostal: liver, pancreas).

los.text: Identify the different parts of the small and large intestines, and describe their locations in the abdomen and list the anatomical differences between them
los.html:
FeatureSmall intestineLarge intestine
PositionCentral, coiledPeripheral frame
Taeniae coliNone3 longitudinal muscle bands
HaustraNoneSacculations
Appendices epiploicaeNoneFat tags
Mucosal foldsPlicae circulares (cross the full width on X-ray)Haustral folds (only part-way across)
MobilityOn a mesenteryAscending/descending retroperitoneal
FeatureJejunumIleum
PositionUpper leftLower right
WallThicker, wider, redderThinner, paler
Vasa rectaLongShort
ArcadesFew (1–2)Many
Mesenteric fatLessMore
Lymphoid tissueLittlePeyer's patches
Duodenum(25 cm, 4 parts)Superior (L1), descending (L2, major papilla), horizontal (L3, crossed by SMA/SMV), ascending (L2) → DJ flexure.
Jejunum ~2/5 and ileum ~3/5 of the rest of the small bowel (~6 m in total).
Large bowelCaecum, appendix, ascending, transverse, descending, sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal.

los.text: Identify abdominal organs on suitable radiographs or MRI scans and recognise common abnormalities
los.html:
AXR basicsSmall bowel central with valvulae conniventes crossing the whole lumen; colon peripheral with haustra crossing part-way.
3-6-9 ruleDilated if small bowel >3 cm, colon >6 cm, caecum >9 cm.
PneumoperitoneumFree air under the diaphragm on an erect CXR; Rigler's sign (both sides of the bowel wall visible) on AXR.
Sigmoid volvulus"coffee bean" loop pointing to the right upper quadrant.
Toxic megacolonTransverse colon >6 cm in colitis.
CalcificationRenal stones (~90% radio-opaque), gallstones (~10–15% visible), calcified AAA wall.
Also look atBones, psoas outlines, soft tissue organ shadows, gas pattern.
CT/MRIAxial slices are viewed from the feet, so the patient's right is on the viewer's left.
